claims: A Silver Alert is a public notification system used in the U.S. to locate missing seniors, particularly those with Alzheimer’s, dementia, or other cognitive impairments.
Silver Alerts are activated by law enforcement.
Silver Alerts broadcast information via media and emergency systems to find at-risk individuals, usually aged 60-65 or older.
A 31-second video from NBC Connecticut on YouTube dated May 6, 2025 explains the purpose of a Silver Alert.
Silver Alert activation generally requires the missing person to have a diagnosed cognitive impairment.
Silver Alert activation generally requires the missing person to be over a certain age, typically 60 or 65 depending on state law.
Silver Alert activation generally requires the missing person to be considered in danger.
Silver Alerts are similar to AMBER Alerts.
Silver Alerts use media outlets, highway signs, and emergency alerts to inform the public.
There have been few independent evaluations of the real-world effectiveness of Silver Alerts.
Some, including this YouTube video, point out that families may face stigma or blame when a loved one with dementia wanders.
